id_and_class.summary: Helen Yetter-Chappell develops a quasi-Berkeleyan realist idealism without God: reality is a vast unity of conscious experience that holds together experiences of every object from every perspective, keeping the world stable when no one is looking. She combines this with a defense of epiphenomenalist dualism, on which individual experiences are causally inert yet are the very stuff of reality.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Reality as a Godless Unity of Experience

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the fundamental constituent of reality. The world is one unified experience that includes experiences as of every object from every perspective, woven, in Yetter-Chappell's image, out of experiential threads.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Within her dualist framework, brain processes give rise to experiences that do not act back on the physical world, and behavior is fully explained physically. In her idealism, the physical world itself is constituted by the unified experience, governed by laws like those of materialist metaphysics.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (consciousness is the fundamental constituent of reality, not an emergent property)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Our perceptions are not representations but literal overlaps with the universal consciousness that makes up reality, so we are in direct contact with the world.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Colors, shapes and sounds are not inner copies of the world; they are woven into the fabric of reality itself, so the world fundamentally is as it appears.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A single, non-agentive unity of experience that need not be omnipotent, omniscient or good and need have no beliefs, desires or intentions; individual conscious experiences; physical laws that govern the regularity of experience.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through direct acquaintance. Yetter-Chappell argues that direct acquaintance with reality only makes sense if reality is fundamentally phenomenal, which gives idealism an optimistic account of our ability to understand the world.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Experiences as of every object from every perspective, bound into one unified experience; individual minds' perceptions are overlapping parts of it.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Perception, the persistence and stability of the physical world, phenomenal self-knowledge, and mental causation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Berkeley's God is stripped to the one feature needed for a stable world: a unified experience that encompasses all aspects of every object, such as the cake in a closed fridge.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness is universal: the whole of reality is one unity of experience, and individual minds are parts that overlap with it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Individual experiences are causally inert; physical processes alone explain behavior. Consciousness matters because it is what reality is made of, not because it causes physical events.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: The universal experience binds together experiences of every object from every perspective into one whole.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Perception is not representation. Perceptual experiences are constituents of the world, which preserves direct realist intuitions.
core_claims_and_evidence: Something outside us must sustain objects when unperceived and explain the regularity of perception, but it need not be a god or even an agent.
Yetter-Chappell argues that the ‘paradox of phenomenal judgment’ for epiphenomenalism arises only when dualism is combined with a physicalist view of the self.
Direct acquaintance with reality is intelligible only if reality is fundamentally phenomenal, against naïve realists.
Individual experiences can be causally inert while consciousness as a whole is the substance of reality.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: conceptual argument in metaphysics and epistemology, building the strongest versions of rival views for comparison.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Combining epiphenomenalist dualism, where brains give rise to experiences, with an idealism where experience is the whole of reality looks contradictory at first. Epiphenomenalism also faces the paradox of phenomenal judgment: how we can know experiences that cause nothing.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: How a non-agentive unity of experience secures the lawful regularity of the world, a job Berkeley assigned to God.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Yetter-Chappell reconciles the two halves by treating individual experiences as causally inert parts of an overarching conscious reality. Whether that fully dissolves the tension between them is open.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The unity of experience that grounds reality has no desires, intentions or agency, so it supplies no cosmic purpose.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: The View From Everywhere: Realist Idealism Without God, Helen Yetter-Chappell
